extracted.intended_audience: State Departments of Transportation (State DOTs), Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs), FHWA staff, and other stakeholders implementing or responding to 23 CFR part 490 GHG performance requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Implementing and reporting the FHWA greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions performance measure for the National Highway System (NHS), including target setting, data collection, calculation, reporting, and FHWA significant-progress assessments under 23 CFR part 490.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG measure definition
rubrics_metrics.description: One measure is used to assess GHG emissions, which is the percent change in tailpipe CO2 emissions on the NHS compared to the reference year (referred to as the GHG measure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The measure is the percent change in on-road tailpipe CO2 emissions on the NHS relative to the reference year; it is part of the NHS performance measures in §490.507(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference year
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference year is calendar year 2022 for the purpose of the GHG measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reference year (CY 2022) is used as the denominator/baseline in calculating percent change; HPMS and other data for the reference year are specified elsewhere (e.g., HPMS data as of Nov 30, 2023 represent reference-year performance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to NHS mainline highways
rubrics_metrics.description: The Greenhouse Gas (GHG) measure in §490.507(b) is applicable to all mainline highways on the Interstate and non-Interstate NHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA authority and the measure apply only to the Interstate System and the non-Interstate NHS; the rule applies to the 50 States, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico.

rubrics_metrics.name: State DOT target types and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs will establish 2- and 4-year statewide emissions reduction targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State DOTs must set both 2-year and 4-year declining CO2 targets for the GHG measure (§490.105(c)(5)); initial/phase-in timing exceptions described elsewhere (e.g., 2024 phase-in).

rubrics_metrics.name: MPO target types and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: MPOs will establish 4-year emissions reduction targets for their metropolitan planning areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPOs with NHS mileage within their metropolitan planning areas must set 4-year declining targets; certain MPOs have additional joint-target requirements when planning areas overlap UZAs (see joint targets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declining-target requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs and MPOs are required to establish declining targets for reducing CO2 emissions generated by on-road mobile sources on the NHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA does not mandate a specific target magnitude — jurisdictions have flexibility to set targets appropriate for their communities and policy priorities, provided targets aim to reduce emissions over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint MPO UZA targets
rubrics_metrics.description: When the metropolitan planning area boundaries of two or more MPOs overlap any portion of an Urbanized Area (UZA) (population 50,000 or more) and the UZA contains NHS mileage, those MPOs will establish joint 4-year targets for that UZA in addition to each MPO's target for their metropolitan planning area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This joint target is established in addition to each MPO's individual metropolitan planning area target; 'urbanized area' per 23 U.S.C. 101(a)(36).

rubrics_metrics.name: Target establishment and reporting deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs will first establish targets and report those targets by February 1, 2024; subsequent targets will be established and reported no later than October 1, 2026, with biennial reports thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These dates set the initial and subsequent target/reporting schedule; see §490.105 and §490.107 for detailed reporting cycle and phase-in rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirement (progress and biennial reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs and MPOs are required to report on their progress in meeting the targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports include State Biennial Performance Reports (per §490.107) and MPO reporting as required; report content, frequency, and publicizing requirements are further specified in §490.107 (e.g., reporting start date, MPO report content, biennial cycle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data requirements — CO2 factors posting
rubrics_metrics.description: The FHWA will post on the FHWA website, no later than August 15th of each reporting year, the CO2 factors for each on-road fuel type that will be used to calculate the GHG metric for the GHG measure in §490.105(c)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdictions must use FHWA-posted CO2 factors for calculations in the applicable reporting year; see §490.509(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data requirements — fuel sales reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Fuel sales information needed to calculate the fuel consumed for the GHG measure shall represent the total number of gallons of fuel consumed by fuel type and be based on fuels sales data for the prior calendar year, and reported to Fuels & FASH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fuel sales data must be comprehensive by fuel type, reference the prior calendar year, and be submitted via Fuels & FASH as specified in §490.509(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data requirements — VMT
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual vehicle miles traveled (VMT) needed to calculate the GHG measure shall come from the best available data that represents the prior calendar year and is consistent, to the maximum extent practicable, with data submitted to HPMS; the VMT data needed for the reference year shall be the HPMS data as of November 30, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use HPMS-consistent VMT to the extent practicable; explicit HPMS extraction dates are used for reference-year and reporting-year comparisons (§490.509(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of tailpipe CO2 emissions (GHG metric) — units and rounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailpipe CO2 emissions on the NHS for a given year shall be computed in million metric tons (mmt) and rounded to the nearest hundredth as specified in §490.511(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The calculation uses fuel consumed by fuel type, CO2 factors, NHS VMT and Total VMT; results are reported in State Biennial Performance Reports and must address reference year and prior year time periods (§490.511(c),(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Variables in GHG metric calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Variables include: (Fuel Consumed)_t = quantity of total annual fuel consumed for on-road fuel type t; (CO2 Factor)_t = amount of CO2 released per unit of fuel consumed for on-road fuel type t; NHS VMT = annual total vehicle-miles traveled on NHS; Total VMT = annual total vehicle-miles traveled on all public roads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These variables feed the formula in §490.511(c); jurisdictions must assemble fuel consumption, CO2 factors, and VMT to compute tailpipe CO2 emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of the GHG measure (percent change) — rounding
rubrics_metrics.description: The GHG measure specified in §490.507(b) shall be computed to the nearest tenth of a percent using the tailpipe CO2 emissions on the NHS for the calendar year and the reference year (CY 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percent-change calculation compares (Tailpipe CO2 Emissions on NHS)_CY to (Tailpipe CO2 Emissions on NHS)_reference year and is rounded to the nearest 0.1% (§490.513(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: MPO calculation flexibility and acceptable methods
rubrics_metrics.description: MPOs are granted additional flexibility in how they calculate the GHG metric: MPOs may use the MPO share of the State's VMT as a proxy for the MPO share of CO2 emissions in the State, VMT estimates along with MOVES emissions factors, FHWA's EERPAT model, or other method the MPO can demonstrate has valid and useful results for CO2 measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPOs may select from listed methods (MPO share of VMT proxy, MOVES with VMT estimates, EERPAT) or justify alternate methods with demonstrated validity (§490.511(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted emissions models and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: MOVES (EPA), EMFAC (California), and FHWA's EERPAT model are referenced for emissions analysis and are permissible tools for estimating emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MOVES may be used with MPO VMT estimates; EMFAC is noted for California; EERPAT is FHWA's tool — MPOs and State DOTs may use these as appropriate per §490.511(d) and related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: HPMS data extraction and acceptance rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The HPMS performance data used for baseline, prior-year, and reference-year calculations shall be the data contained within HPMS on November 30th of the year the Baseline Period Performance Report is due to FHWA; HPMS data as of Nov 30, 2023 represents reference year performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a State DOT's reported data are not accepted in Fuels & FASH or HPMS by the specified data extraction date, the State DOT's reported data are not accepted for the GHG measure (§490.509 and related paragraphs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant progress assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA will assess whether State DOTs have made significant progress toward achieving their targets for the GHG measure and will make determinations on significant progress consistent with §§490.107 and 490.109 provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the midpoint of the performance period, FHWA conducts significant-progress determinations; phase-in rules for 2024 may affect mid-period determinations for 2-year targets; see §490.109 and §490.107 for criteria, timing, and classification of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences when significant progress is not made
rubrics_metrics.description: If significant progress is not made for the target established for the GHG measure in §490.105(c)(5), then the State DOT shall document the actions it will take to achieve the GHG performance target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA does not impose an automatic penalty; the identified consequence in the rule is documentation of corrective actions by the State DOT (§490.107 and related sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in provisions for 2024 reporting period
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain requirements apply only after the submittal of the 2024 Mid Performance Period Progress Report: (i) State DOTs are not required to establish a 2-year target for 2024, (ii) FHWA shall not make a determination of significant progress toward 2-year targets at the midpoint, and (iii) FHWA will classify the assessment of progress as 'progress not determined' and exclude them from certain requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These phase-in rules temporarily exclude 2-year-target mid-period determinations and reporting for the initial cycle; see §490.107(e)(6) for full details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units, rounding, and reporting precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailpipe CO2 emissions are computed in million metric tons (mmt) and rounded to the nearest hundredth; the GHG measure percent change is computed to the nearest tenth of a percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to unit and rounding precision in calculations and in State Biennial Performance Reports (§490.511(c), §490.513(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Greenhouse gas' for the regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Greenhouse gas (GHG) is any gas that absorbs infrared radiation (traps heat) in the atmosphere. Approximately 97 percent of on-road GHG emissions are carbon dioxide (CO2) from burning fossil fuel. Other transportation GHGs are methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), and hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed GHG measure specifically applies to CO2 as the predominant on-road GHG; other gases are acknowledged but CO2 is the focus (§490.505 definition and footnotes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting time periods to address
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculations shall be reported in the State Biennial Performance Reports and shall address the reference year and the calendar year preceding the reporting year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State reports must include GHG metric calculations for the reference year (CY 2022) and prior-year comparisons as specified in §490.511(f) and §490.107 reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: FHWA posting and data transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA will post required CO2 factors and supporting data/tools (e.g., CO2 factors by Aug 15) to ensure consistent calculation inputs across jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA's posted materials are authoritative for the reporting year and intended to improve consistency and transparency of GHG calculations (§490.509(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on FHWA authority and non-prescriptiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA is only requiring that State DOTs and MPOs establish declining targets for GHG emissions on the NHS; FHWA is neither requiring any specific targets nor mandating any penalties for failing to achieve these targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule is structured to provide oversight and reporting (targets, progress assessments) but leaves target level and many methodological choices to State DOTs and MPOs within specified constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of specified paragraphs (including those implementing the GHG measure) are separate and severable from one another and from the other provisions of this part; if any provision is stayed or determined invalid, the remaining provisions shall continue in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule expressly lists those sections considered severable in §490.515 to preserve the remainder of the part if any portion is invalidated.
